newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES MIXED AS SHORTAGE EASES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MKT RATES MIXED AS SHORTAGE EASES.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to softer on Thursday morning, reflecting an easing in cash shortage in the system, dealers said.
"The market shortage seems to be coming down as people recover from the statutory reserve payments made earlier in the week," one dealer said.
He said dealers were purchasing 91-day treasury bills at 20.21 percent from the central Reserve Bank and selling them in the market at 20.15 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 23 and 22 percent respectively, down from 24 and 23 percent but bankers acceptance bills held steady at 22.75 and 22 percent.
Call money eased to 23 percent from 24 percent, with the central bank indicating a start-off market deficit of Z$50 million, an improvement on Wednesday's Z$119 million shortage.
